content: Always ask for direct confirmation before starting any implementation or writing code. Never begin coding without explicit approval.
Before building or debugging, always check relevant memories first — they may have rules, gotchas, or patterns that prevent mistakes.

Before starting execution of any plan or sub-phase, present a pre-flight brief that flags questionable items, speculative/premature work, and things needing explicit confirmation before coding. Do not treat draft plans as frozen specs. Sub-phases are individual design decisions — colors, data formats, component structures, text labels, interaction patterns. Never bundle multiple unconfirmed decisions into one batch. If a single edit changes more than one independent thing, pause and verify each choice separately before coding.

Don't let "it's small" or "it's just one field" shortcut proper abstraction. When something conceptually belongs in its own type or layer, build it from day one — even if it duplicates a few lines. The size of the change is not the measure; the clarity of the abstraction is.
User wants rigorous pushback during brainstorming, not agreement-seeking, and prefers best-solution tradeoff analysis.
User prefers removing obsolete compatibility wrappers instead of keeping tech debt.
